prompt.context: Copier, Co. is a national distributor of office equipment, particularly commercial-grade copiers. The firm sells the equipment directly to companies for use in their offices, as well as provides regular service including maintenance, repairs, and replacing disposable parts.
prompt.question: Recently, the company has experienced declining profit margins. We have been hired to determine why this is happening and what to do to reverse the trend.

clarifying_info.q: How does the sales process work?
clarifying_info.a: The company bids on contracts; contracts are typically awarded to the lowest bidder. The bid consists of a per-copier cost which includes 1 year of maintenance as part of the sales price. Salesmen have free reign to determine bid price and are compensated based on commission (% of overall sales).

There is one major competitor (American Copiers) and a new, low-cost competitor (Bottom Dollar Copier) that has recently entered the market. All three companies are distributors and service technicians, not manufacturers.

clarifying_info.q: What product are we focusing on?
clarifying_info.a: The case will focus on one identical copier sold and distributed by multiple firms.

exhibits.title: Copiers in Order vs. Bid Price for Copier Co
exhibits.shows: Scatter plot with number of copiers in order on the x-axis (ranging roughly 5–35) and average bid price per copier on the y-axis (ranging roughly $2,000–$6,000), plotting individual contracts for Copier Co.
exhibits.data: X-axis: Number of Copiers in Order (5 to 35); Y-axis: Average Bid Price per Copier ($2,000 to $6,000); data points show a general downward trend as order size increases, with a few high-price outliers

exhibits.title: Copier Co Successful Bid Info by Competitor Scenario
exhibits.shows: Table comparing three bidding scenarios: competing against American Copier only, competing against Bottom Dollar Copier only, and competing against both. Shows average bid price, average copiers in order, cost of copier, service cost per page printed, and average pages printed per copier per month.
exhibits.data: Competing vs. American Copier only: Avg Bid Price $5,000, Avg Copiers 20, Cost of Copier $3,000, Service cost $0.05/page, Pages printed 1,000/month/copier, service 1 year included. Competing vs. Bottom Dollar Copier only: Avg Bid Price $4,000, Avg Copiers 25, same cost/service. Competing vs. both: Avg Bid Price $3,000, Avg Copiers 30, same cost/service.

framework: Revenue drivers: Volume (number of copiers sold / contracts awarded) and Price (average bid price per copier)
Cost drivers – Fixed: sales force base salaries, warehousing, overhead
Cost drivers – Variable: service/labor costs, COGS, transportation, sales force commission
Non-financial / external factors: competitive landscape (American Copiers, Bottom Dollar Copier), bidding process dynamics
Non-financial / internal factors: salesforce compensation structure (commission % of sales), product mix

questions.prompt: Walk through your framework for diagnosing the declining profit margins.
questions.guidance: Candidate should use a profitability framework (Profit = Revenue – Costs), breaking revenue into volume and price and costs into fixed vs. variable. Strong candidates also surface non-financial factors: the competitive bidding process, the new low-cost entrant, and the commission-based compensation incentive for salespeople.

questions.prompt: You have been shown Exhibit 1 (bid price vs. order size). What do you observe and what hypotheses does this generate?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify a negative correlation: larger orders have lower per-copier bid prices. A good candidate hypothesizes that salespeople may be lowering bid prices on large contracts to earn higher total commission (volume effect outweighs margin compression). A great candidate also notes the few high-price outliers and asks whether those correspond to contracts with fewer competitors, setting up Exhibit 2.

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 2, calculate the profit per copier and total profit for contracts won against American Copier only. Then assess whether the other scenarios are profitable.
questions.guidance: Candidate must annualize pages printed (1,000 pages/month x 12 months = 12,000 pages/year). Service cost per copier = 12,000 x $0.05 = $600. Contribution per copier = Bid Price – COGS. Profit per copier = Contribution – Service cost. Common pitfall: using monthly pages without multiplying by 12, or forgetting service is included for only 1 year. For the all-three-competitor scenario, candidates should recognize the contribution margin is zero and therefore the contract is unprofitable once service costs are included.

math.setup: For each scenario: Contribution per copier = Avg Bid Price – Cost of Copier. Service cost per copier = 1,000 pages/month x 12 months x $0.05/page = $600. Profit per copier = Contribution – Service cost. Total Profit = Profit per copier x Avg Copiers in Order.
steps: Scenario 1 (vs. American Copier only): Contribution = $5,000 – $3,000 = $2,000; Service cost = $600; Profit per copier = $1,400; Total Profit = $1,400 x 20 = $28,000
Scenario 2 (vs. Bottom Dollar Copier only): Contribution = $4,000 – $3,000 = $1,000; Service cost = $600; Profit per copier = $400; Total Profit = $400 x 25 = $10,000
Scenario 3 (vs. both A.C. and B.D.C.): Contribution = $3,000 – $3,000 = $0; Service cost = $600; Profit per copier = –$600; Total Profit = –$600 x 30 = –$18,000
math.answer: Scenario 1: $28,000 profit; Scenario 2: $10,000 profit; Scenario 3: –$18,000 loss

questions.prompt: Brainstorm solutions to the low-bid / low-margin problem. Management wants to continue bidding on all contracts.
questions.guidance: Candidate should generate a variety of levers across pricing controls, incentive redesign, cost reduction, and revenue enhancement. Simply recommending 'don't bid' is insufficient since management wants to pursue all contracts.

questions.prompt: The CEO is awaiting your recommendation. What do you tell Copier Co?
questions.guidance: Candidate should concisely identify root causes (new low-cost competitor driving down win prices, plus commission-based compensation incentivizing salespeople to underbid on large contracts) and propose one or two specific, actionable solutions with immediate next steps.

brainstorming.prompt: What solutions would you recommend to address the low-margin problem in contracts competed against multiple bidders? Management wants to continue bidding on all contracts.

categories.name: Pricing controls
ideas: Set minimum allowable bid prices for salespeople to prevent unprofitable discounting
Require management approval for bids below a floor price on large contracts

categories.name: Compensation restructuring
ideas: Change salesperson compensation from % of revenue to % of profit or contribution margin
Introduce clawbacks or penalties for contracts that generate negative margin

categories.name: Product / service packaging
ideas: Offer a no-service-included option to lower the bid price floor while protecting margin
Offer multi-year service contracts priced separately to shift service revenue out of the initial bid

categories.name: Cost reduction
ideas: Negotiate better COGS pricing with copier manufacturers given volume
Reduce per-page service costs through efficiency improvements or renegotiated parts pricing

categories.name: Revenue diversification
ideas: Bundle complementary products (paper, toner, other office equipment) to increase total contract value
Offer value-added services (training, fleet analytics) to differentiate from low-cost competitors

categories.name: Market / competitor strategy
ideas: Pursue joint ventures with competitors on very large orders to share service burden and stabilize pricing
Selectively target contract segments where Bottom Dollar Copier is less competitive (e.g., premium service requirements)

recommendation: Copier Co's declining margins are primarily caused by two reinforcing factors: the entry of Bottom Dollar Copier forcing bid prices down on contested contracts, and a commission-on-revenue compensation structure that incentivizes salespeople to underbid large orders to maximize their total payout.
Immediate priority: restructure salesperson compensation to tie commissions to profit margin rather than revenue, and establish minimum bid-price floors to prevent negative-contribution contracts.
risks: If minimum bid floors are set too high, Copier Co may lose large contracts entirely to competitors.
Changing compensation structure may cause short-term salesperson attrition or resistance.
Bottom Dollar Copier may continue undercutting even cost-of-copier levels, suggesting they have a different cost structure or are pursuing market-share-at-a-loss strategy.
next_steps: Analyze the full contract portfolio to quantify how many contracts are currently bid against both competitors and their aggregate profit impact.
Design a revised compensation plan (e.g., % of gross profit per contract) and model its effect on salesperson earnings to manage change resistance.
Pilot minimum bid-price floors on a regional basis and monitor win-rate and margin impact before rolling out nationally.
